title: docker on linux: rootless podman cannot bind a low port / map subuid
scenario: On linux, a docker workload is broken: rootless podman cannot bind a low port / map subuid. Diagnostics show 'rootlessport / permission denied binding :80'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'podman_rootless' for docker on linux
expected_reasoning: Rootless containers cannot bind <1024 by default and depend on subuid/subgid ranges.
Either publish to a high port + reverse proxy, or grant the capability deliberately.
Verify /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid ranges exist for the user.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'rootless podman cannot bind a low port / map subuid' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('podman_rootless') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Fall back to running podman as root, defeating rootless isolation.
Miss that /etc/subuid has no range for the user.
hints: net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start lets rootless bind lower ports.
subuid/subgid ranges are required for the user namespace mapping.
reference_solution: Publish high port + proxy, or lower unprivileged port start
Verify the container runs and is reachable
alternative_solution: Run the container in a systemd user unit (podman generate systemd) with the right lingering setup.
edge_cases: cgroups v1 host cannot do rootless resource limits; v2 is required.
goal: Il container/servizio docker ha un problema: rootless podman cannot bind a low port / map subuid. Ripristina lo stato desiderato risolvendo la causa.
